To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of lactic acid during the growth phase is linked to the production rate and the growth rate, and that the part of the final amount that is produced during growth depends on the growth conditions.
the part of latic acid produced during the growth-associated phase is mainly controlled by the growth rate and by the undissociated acid concentration in the media.

the part of latic acid produced during the growth phase of Lactobalillus helveticous is mainly controlled by culture conditions (media compo- sition, pH, lactat and undissociate lactic acid concentration), and not by seed culture conditions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lactic acid production by the lactic acid bacteria is a complex process, which depends on several factors and is affected by many different conditions.
the growth-associated production is not the most efficient way of lactic acid production, but the most convenient one.
the lactic acid production by L. helve- ticus is linked with growth during the deceleration phase, and partially linked during the associated phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth-associated and deceleration phases of L. helvéticus are not independent and the production during the deceleration phase is not only due to a non-growth associated mechanism.
, for the optimization of the lactic fermentation, the associated and the subsequent deceler- ation phases must be considered.
the production of lactic acid by L. helve- ticus during the growth-associated phase is linked to biomass growth and that the part of latic acid produced is controlled by the culture con- di- tions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production rate of lactic acid by L. helveti- cus is mainly controlled by culture conditions, whereas the growth-associated production rate is mainly controlled by the seed culture conditions.
